A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

content.text: I'll start by listing the tables and their schemas.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, service_name, attr_span_kind, count(*) n, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), avg(duration)/1e6, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: Checkout and shipping show large latency increases, and accounting's internal spans are up too. Next I'll check the status codes and the per-pod breakdown for the affected services.

content.text: Uptimes are all continuous with no restarts, so no pod restarted. I'll check whether any hubble metrics exist in either period.

input.query: SELECT 'sum_ab' t, metric, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE metric ILIKE '%hubble%' OR metric ILIKE '%network%' GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'sum_norm', metric, count(*) FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE metric ILIKE '%hubble%' OR metric ILIKE '%network%' GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'm_ab', metric, count(*) FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric ILIKE '%hubble%' OR metric ILIKE '%network%' GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'm_norm', metric, count(*) FROM normal_metrics WHERE metric ILIKE '%hubble%' OR metric ILIKE '%network%' GROUP BY ALL

content.text: Hubble metrics are absent from both periods, so the evidence has to come from spans, logs and pod metrics. Next I'll check the logs and the per-pod resource metrics.

input.query: SELECT service_name, level, attr_log_template, count(*) n FROM abnormal_logs GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY n DESC

content.text: The logs contain no error-level entries. I'll read the accounting, shipping and checkout messages to see what they say.

input.query: SELECT service_name, level, message, count(*) n FROM abnormal_logs WHERE service_name IN ('accounting','shipping','checkout','quote','fraud-detection','') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY n DESC

content.text: A kubelet event shows the accounting container in a back-off restart loop, which the uptime data didn't reveal. I'll check the container restart counters and resource metrics for accounting.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, metric, service_name, count(*) n, round(avg(value),2) avg_v, round(min(value),2) min_v, round(max(value),2) max_v FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.memory.usage','container.memory.usage','container.cpu.utilization','k8s.container.cpu_limit_utilization','jvm.memory.used','jvm.gc.duration') AND service_name='accounting' GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, service_name, count(*), round(avg(value),2), round(min(value),2), round(max(value),2) FROM normal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.memory.usage','container.memory.usage','container.cpu.utilization','k8s.container.cpu_limit_utilization','jvm.memory.used','jvm.gc.duration') AND service_name='accounting' GROUP BY ALL

content.text: Accounting's memory dips to 66 MB in the incident window against about 119 MB normally, which fits a restart. I'll list the other metrics recorded for accounting to see what else is there.

input.query: SELECT metric, count(*) n FROM (SELECT metric, service_name FROM abnormal_metrics UNION ALL SELECT metric, service_name FROM abnormal_metrics_sum) WHERE service_name='accounting' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1

content.text: There is no restart counter, so I'll use CPU and memory over time to judge whether accounting is actually failing. I'll also compare CPU across the services on the request path.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, service_name, metric, round(avg(value),3) avg_v, round(max(value),3) max_v, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.pod.cpu.usage','k8s.pod.memory_limit_utilization') AND service_name IN ('accounting','shipping','quote','checkout','frontend','fraud-detection','postgresql') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, metric, round(avg(value),3), round(max(value),3), count(*) FROM normal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.pod.cpu.usage','k8s.pod.memory_limit_utilization') AND service_name IN ('accounting','shipping','quote','checkout','frontend','fraud-detection','postgresql') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: Accounting's CPU is up and its memory is down, consistent with a restart loop. But nothing synchronous calls accounting, so its effect appears to stay inside accounting. Next I'll check whether the shipping-to-quote path shows network-level symptoms such as errors or drops.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, service_name, metric, round(avg(value),2) avg_v, round(max(value),2) max_v, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE service_name IN ('shipping','quote','checkout') AND metric IN ('k8s.pod.network.errors','k8s.pod.network.io','system.network.dropped','system.network.errors') GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, metric, round(avg(value),2), round(max(value),2), count(*) FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE service_name IN ('shipping','quote','checkout') AND metric IN ('k8s.pod.network.errors','k8s.pod.network.io','system.network.dropped','system.network.errors') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: Network counters are flat on the shipping, quote and checkout pods, so this does not look like a network fault. Next I'll check which user-facing endpoints slowed down, using frontend server spans grouped by route.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' p, service_name, span_name, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,1) avg_ms, round(max(duration)/1e6,1) max_ms FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('frontend','frontend-proxy') AND attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, span_name, count(*), round(avg(duration)/1e6,1), round(max(duration)/1e6,1) FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('frontend','frontend-proxy') AND attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 3,2,1

content.text: The user-visible impact is concentrated on `POST /api/checkout` (about 701 ms against 25 ms normal), while other frontend routes are flat. Next I'll join spans within traces to confirm the call chain shipping → checkout → frontend.

input.query: SELECT c.service_name caller, c.span_name caller_span, c.attr_span_kind ck, s.service_name callee, s.span_name callee_span, s.attr_span_kind sk, count(*) n, round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,1) caller_ms, round(avg(s.duration)/1e6,1) callee_ms FROM abnormal_traces c JOIN abnormal_traces s ON c.trace_id=s.trace_id AND s.parent_span_id=c.span_id WHERE c.service_name<>s.service_name GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY n DESC
